correctness.rationale: The dichotomy construction is valid. The focal characterization supplies a nowhere differentiable Lipschitz seed in every negative case; subtracting its endpoint affine interpolant preserves nowhere differentiability and gives zero endpoints. Scaled copies on adjacent dyadic intervals retain the same Lipschitz constant. The quasi-triangle inequality gives the cross-interval upper estimate \(\operatorname{Lip}(T(a))\le\kappa L\|a\|_\infty\), while restriction to each support gives \(L\|a\|_\infty\le\operatorname{Lip}(T(a))\), even when the supremum is not attained. Thus \(T\) is an isomorphic embedding of \(\ell_\infty\) with closed range, and any nonzero coefficient forces nondifferentiability throughout the corresponding interval.
